goal: Hydrate T-KRP-D with repo-local research and explore evidence before governed delivery.
topic: Orchestrator assumption-surfacing checkpoint at goal classification

local_sources.use: Establishes Karpathy initiative boundaries, thin-layer precedent, D23 relevance, and deferral of T-KRP-D.
Establishes the injectable skill boundary and reserves orchestrator goal-classification policy for T-KRP-D.
Establishes builder-only boundary and defers orchestrator assumption surfacing to T-KRP-D.
Provides the repo-local assumption-surfacing discipline and explicit T-KRP-D boundary.
Canonical authored orchestrator posture surface and existing Stage 0 classification contract.
D23 routing contract that should consume better classification inputs rather than be replaced.
Stage 0 classification schema, Declaration flow, gate-write order, and run-ledger expectations.
Concrete routing rows and classification dimensions affected by T-KRP-D.
Confirms T-KRP-D title, M1 target layer, governed delivery pipeline, and INI-KRP-001 placement.

implications_for_azoth: T-KRP-D should turn goal classification into a falsifiable checkpoint that names assumptions before composing a pipeline.
The checkpoint belongs between context recall/repo evidence read-back and the Declaration, so the human sees uncertainty before approval.
The checkpoint should explain why the classification is known-pattern, needs-research, novel, instruction-refinement, or otherwise routed.
Auto-router should remain the routing table; T-KRP-D should improve the quality of inputs to D23 rather than replace it.
Generated mirrors are projection targets only after the future governed implementation edits canonical source.

explore_findings.blast_radius: RED if generated mirrors are counted; YELLOW if only authored canonical surfaces are counted.
implementation_risks: Editing generated mirrors directly can create deploy parity drift.
Changing auto-router or auto.pipeline.yaml changes D23 routing behavior and needs focused router tests.
.claude/commands/auto.md is the current authored body source referenced by commands/auto/command.yaml.
Assumption surfacing can broaden into a governance rule; keep it an orchestrator classification checkpoint unless re-scoped.

recommended_scope: Hydrate .azoth/roadmap-specs/v0.2.0/T-KRP-D.yaml as a governed M1 spec.
Scope future implementation to canonical orchestrator posture around Stage 0 goal classification.
Specify an assumption checkpoint output that captures goal interpretation, owned surfaces, out-of-scope surfaces, evidence basis, uncertainty, and classification rationale.
Require the checkpoint to feed Declaration rationale and auto-router classification.
Require generated mirror refresh and deploy parity checks only in the later implementation slice.
non_goals: No implementation edits in this planning hydration session.
No manual edits to generated orchestrator mirrors.
No new governance or Trust Contract semantics unless separately scoped and approved.
acceptance_seeds: T-KRP-D spec exists and references this context pack plus prior T-KRP-A/B/C capsules.
Spec identifies target_layer: M1 and delivery_pipeline: governed.
Spec names canonical orchestrator source as the authored implementation surface.
Spec requires a pre-Declaration assumption checkpoint during goal classification.
Checkpoint covers scope, risk, complexity, knowledge, evidence basis, uncertainty, gates, owned surfaces, and deferrals.
Future implementation adds concise comments in authored surfaces and parity tests explaining the T-KRP-D/D23 handoff boundary.
Future validation includes azoth-deploy parity checks and targeted agent/template tests.
comment_handoff: Do not edit parallel implementation-session files just to add comments from this planning session.
Carry the comment requirement forward in the T-KRP-D spec so the future implementation can add comments in the same scoped slice as the behavior change.
Comments should explain that the checkpoint improves inputs to auto-router and does not replace D23 or implement T-KRP-E.
